briefing:
# Pre-Meeting Briefing: Databricks, 17 November 2026

**Scope:** News, launches, deals, and hires from roughly 18 October to 17 November 2026, based only on the search results provided. I found no sources on hires.

## What changed

**Financials (unaudited)**
- Databricks reportedly passed a $7B revenue run rate, growing 80% year over year. Its Lakehouse product is above $1.5B (growing over 100%), and Lakebase is above $100M. These figures come from Ben Horowitz's 27 October essay, and Databricks is private, so they are not audited (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-horowitz-says-databricks-hit-7b-as-agents-outquery-people). Horowitz also said agents now send Databricks more queries than people do (https://fourweekmba.com/ai-horowitz-says-databricks-hit-7b-as-agents-outquery-people).
- The company was most recently valued at $190B. It has no announced IPO date and no public S-1 as of October 2026 (https://smartasset.com/investing/databricks-ipo-date-timeline-valuation-and-investment-options).

**Launches**
- On 11 November, Databricks launched a set of agentic AI tools. An updated Genie assistant works in the background, proactively surfacing suggestions, and a new "Ontology" feature scans an organization's data (https://finance.yahoo.com/technology/ai/articles/day-anthropic-office-push-databricks-220704968.html).
- Native Genie plugins were also launched on 11 November for ChatGPT, Claude, Microsoft Copilot Cowork, and Grok Bot. Other compatible agents can connect through the Genie One MCP server (https://www.unite.ai/databricks-launches-native-genie-plugins-for-four-ai-agents).

**Deals and partnerships**
- HP is moving its customer data platform into Databricks, with a stated target of 40% lower costs (https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/2026/10/20/hp-moves-customer-data-platform-into-databricks-eyes-40-lower-costs).
- Databricks plans a $3B investment in Europe and the Middle East. The only detail available is a headline in a press-release list (https://www.hpcwire.com/bigdatawire/2026/10/20/hp-moves-customer-data-platform-into-databricks-eyes-40-lower-costs).
- Commvault announced "Data Activate for Databricks," which makes governed enterprise data available for analytics and AI. Early access is planned for December 2026 in select Azure regions. This is a Commvault announcement, not a Databricks one (https://www.tradingview.com/news/tradingview:a912a3a702a15:0-commvault-cvlt-plans-governed-data-solution-for-databricks-ai).

**Hires:** No sources found.

**Other coverage:** A weekly analytics roundup mentions "updates from Databricks" but gives no detail (https://solutionsreview.com/business-intelligence/analytics-and-data-science-news-for-the-week-of-november-6-updates-from-databricks-ocient-smartsheet-more).

## Caveats
- Revenue figures are self-reported and come through a third-party essay. Treat them as unverified.
- The Commvault item is not yet generally available, and adoption is unreported.
- The company profile lists acquisitions, including Electric DB (August 2026) and Panther Labs (June 2026), but both predate the 30-day window (https://tavily.com/knowledge/company/7LlnrDq1nEGX).

## Open questions
1. The $7B run rate and the claim that agents now outnumber human queries are unaudited. What definitions sit behind them, and can you share the Lakehouse and Lakebase split and the share of growth from agent-driven usage?
2. Which of the new agent capabilities (background Genie, Ontology, and the native plugins for ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, and Grok) will be generally available, and how will governed agent access be priced and controlled for enterprise customers?
3. What does the $3B Europe and Middle East investment mean for data residency and regional capacity, and when will partner integrations such as Commvault's Azure early access reach our regions?
